scenes.heading: Adding and subtracting integers
scenes.sub: What happens when you take away a negative?
scenes.say: What is five take away negative four? It sounds strange, but by the end of this video you'll know it's nine, and why.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Cancelling a bill you owe makes you richer
scenes.science: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding
scenes.breaks: Real banks have cents and limits, but integers are whole numbers that can go as low as you like.
scenes.say: Think of your bank balance. Adding a negative is like getting a bill, so your money goes down. Subtracting a negative is like someone cancelling a bill you owed. Taking away a debt makes you richer, so subtracting a negative is the same as adding.

scenes.heading: Moving on the number line
scenes.say: On a number line, start at the first number. Adding a positive moves you right. Subtracting a positive moves you left. So negative six plus four lands on negative two.
scenes.caption: On a number line, start at the first number. Adding a positive moves you right. Subtracting a positive moves you left. So −6 + 4 lands on −2.

scenes.heading: Jumping on the number line
scenes.say: Here is negative six plus four. First the number line, then a dot at negative six. Adding four means jumping four to the right, so you land on negative two.
scenes.caption: Here is −6 + 4. First the number line, then a dot at −6. Adding 4 means jumping 4 to the right, so you land on −2.

scenes.heading: Change two signs
scenes.say: Here's the key rule. a minus negative b equals a plus b. Two minus signs side by side become a plus. A plus next to a minus becomes a minus. Same signs make plus, different signs make minus.
scenes.caption: Here's the key rule. a − (−b) = a + b. Two minus signs side by side become a plus. A plus next to a minus becomes a minus. Same signs make plus, different signs make minus.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Work out 5 − (−4).
scenes.say: Work out five minus negative four. Look at the signs in the middle: minus, negative. Change two signs, so it becomes five plus four. The answer is nine.
scenes.caption: Work out 5 − (−4). Look at the signs in the middle: minus, negative. Change two signs, so it becomes 5 + 4. The answer is 9.

scenes.heading: Money example
scenes.question: Mia has $40, spends $65, then is given $30. What is her balance?
scenes.say: Mia has forty dollars, spends sixty-five, then her nan gives her thirty. Forty minus sixty-five is negative twenty-five. Then negative twenty-five plus thirty is five. Mia has five dollars.
scenes.caption: Mia has $40, spends $65, then her nan gives her $30. 40 − 65 = −25. Then −25 + 30 = 5. Mia has $5.

scenes.heading: Don't mix these up
scenes.say: Watch out for this one. Negative eight minus six means go six further down, to negative fourteen. Negative eight plus six means go six up, to negative two.
scenes.caption: Watch out for this one. −8 − 6 means go 6 further down, to −14. −8 + 6 means go 6 up, to −2.

points: Check by adding the answer back
scenes.say: Quick recap. Adding moves right, subtracting moves left. Adding a negative is subtracting. Subtracting a negative is adding. And you can always check a subtraction by adding back. Now try the practice questions!
